title: Stine-Morrow (2007): Short-answer practice
instructions: Answer in English with a term, program name, or number. Keep answers concise and use the distinctions made in the article.

items.question: What term describes the capacity for rapid encoding and transformation of novel information?
items.explanation: Mental mechanics tend to decline with age, whereas knowledge-based crystallized abilities may remain stable or increase.

items.question: Which abilities depend on knowledge and the acquisition of culture and may remain stable or increase into late life?
items.explanation: Life experience can strengthen cultural, pragmatic, and knowledge-based competence. Its trajectory differs from that of fluid abilities.

items.question: What form of engagement means implementing task-specific cognitive processes through effective allocation of attention?
items.explanation: Attentional engagement concerns how a person carries out a selected task, rather than which intellectual environments the person habitually selects.

items.question: What form of engagement means habitually selecting intellectually stimulating environmental contexts?
items.explanation: The author proposes that these choices may shape the cognitive system underlying future performance; broad benefits are not established merely by defining engagement.

items.question: What is the abbreviation for the language-processing model involving word, textbase, and situation-model representations?
items.explanation: The SRLP model uses readers' responses to text-processing demands to characterize how they allocate attention.

items.question: In the SRLP model, what regulatory mechanism recruits resources to reduce the gap between perceived comprehension and a reference value?
items.explanation: Figure 1 describes a negative feedback loop: a processor demands more resources when its representation is not good enough, until perceived comprehension satisfies the reference value.

items.question: What term describes a reader's pattern of relative changes in reading time as text-processing demands vary?
items.explanation: Allocation policy is operationalized using relative changes in unit reading times associated with text characteristics. It indexes the quality and extent of attentional engagement.

items.question: What belief concerns whether one can affect the outcomes of memory performance through one's own effort?
items.explanation: Working-memory capacity and memory self-efficacy partly accounted for age differences in responsiveness to an accuracy goal.

items.question: What methodological explanation applies when people with greater inherent vitality are more likely to choose and maintain intellectual activities?
items.explanation: Selection can help explain the correlation between an engaged lifestyle and cognition, so the correlation alone does not establish a causal effect of activity.

items.question: What explanation says that activity, cognition, and dementia vulnerability may correlate because they derive from the same underlying aging process?
items.explanation: The article considers whether these indicators of vitality are biobehavioral markers of a shared, genetically driven aging process.

items.question: What concept describes experience-enriched neural circuitry that supplies alternative repertoires in the presence of pathology?
items.explanation: Cognitive reserve is presented as an explanation for why greater educational attainment may be associated with tolerating brain pathology longer before clinical symptoms appear.

items.question: How many training sessions did the ACTIVE trial provide in memory, processing speed, or reasoning?
items.explanation: Older adults were randomly assigned to training conditions or a no-contact control. Training effects were specific to the abilities trained.

items.question: In the ACTIVE findings cited in this 2007 article, retention of training effects was demonstrated for up to how many years?
items.explanation: Retention was demonstrated for up to five years. Persistence does not imply broad transfer to other abilities or everyday tasks.

items.question: Which intervention for older adults combines ill-defined problems, creativity, collaboration, and choice to simulate an engaged lifestyle?
items.explanation: Senior Odyssey builds on Odyssey of the Mind. Its preliminary findings did not yet establish broad-based improvement in cognitive functioning.

items.question: What hypothesis links cognitive vitality to how people engage with selected activities and the abilities they develop through them?
items.explanation: The conclusion identifies interactions between attentional and activity engagement and their psychosocial mechanisms as questions requiring empirical tests.
